title: POC Weekly Pulse — fallback gating & go decision
next_steps: Liz to send updated pilot pricing matrix and cost-per-1M tokens breakdown by 2027-03-19
Ravi to run 3000-concurrent connection canary test and share traces by 2027-03-21
Customer to authorize short maintenance window for cutover rehearsal on 2027-03-25
action_items: Ravi (SE): Produce end-to-end canary runbook draft — due 2027-03-20
Liz (AE): Share SOC2 + network diagrams + KMS integration guide — due 2027-03-18
Maya (VP Eng): Confirm internal stakeholders for go/no-go call — due 2027-03-19
header_text: Date: 2027-03-17 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62 min | Attendees: Liz Chen, Ravi Kapoor (Redwood); Maya Ortiz, Tomás Rivera, Hannah Li (Crescent) | Recording: Fireflies.ai
summary: Weekly POC sync. Reviewed pilot metrics (latency/cost/errs), discussed canary criteria, fallback plans, security signoffs, and go decision timeline. Agreed to run a scale canary and deliver runbooks + pricing. Action items assigned.
transcript:
00:00 Liz Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we're at 4pm UTC, thanks for making time. quick agenda — results from the pilot burn-in, canary criteria, cutover window and security signoffs.
00:14 Maya Ortiz: sorry delayed start, hopping in now. thanks liz.
00:22 Ravi Kapoor: good morning / afternoon all. i'll start with the perf highlights.
01:05 Ravi Kapoor: so baseline: over the last 48 hours our hosted endpoint saw median p95 latency at ~210ms for 256-token responses, cost per 1k tokens trending at about $0.55 after quantization. there were two spikes, one at 2am caused by a rolling job that sent long context, and one brief GC pause on their side i think.
01:47 Maya Ortiz: when you say quantization did you mean int8 path? because we thought you recommended int8-ggml for cost.
02:05 Ravi Kapoor: yes int8 optimized kernel, though it's not pure ggml — our runtime uses hardware kernels on the cards we provisioned. accuracy delta vs fp16 was within our threshold, like 1.2% BLEU-ish on the eval set, not exact BLEU but you get the idea. transcription note: i said blu uh — small slippage.
02:53 Tomás Rivera: the error budget we care about is really user-facing hallucination rate and regression on our prompts. did you run the regression against the new prompt set we uploaded last week?
03:10 Ravi Kapoor: we re-ran the set against the canary model and the baseline, differences are in the shared spreadsheet. overall quality delta is negligible, there were three prompts with degenerate responses we flagged.
03:42 Hannah Li: quick security note — we need to validate KMS integration and confirm logs are available in our SIEM. also data residency: anything that touches PHI needs to stay in our us-east-1 VPC.
04:05 Liz Chen: yes, KMS integration guide is in the docs we'll share, and point on logs — we stream audit logs to an S3 bucket w/ lifecycle rules and can push to your Splunk via Kinesis. will share network diagram.
04:33 Maya Ortiz: good. on canary criteria — we want to see 72 hours of steady-state with no SLO violations and a throughput test at 2x expected peak. is that aligned?
05:01 Ravi Kapoor: we recommended a progressive ramp: 25% traffic for 12 hours, 50% for 12, then a stress at 200% for a 3-hour window, then full shift if metrics look healthy. Our gating checks are latency p95 < 350ms, error rate <0.5%, and no regression in quality tests beyond agreed threshold.
05:35 Tomás Rivera: can we get the exact metric dashboards? the trimmed down views for infra and for product teams.
05:47 Liz Chen: yes i'll create two dashboard links — infra and product. also add a third view for security with audit/logging toggles.
06:12 Ravi Kapoor: small note — when you do the traffic shaping please include header hints so the runtime can tag sessions for TTL and KV-cash — sorry KV cache — the transcript sometimes says cash.
06:40 Hannah Li: okay, about the maintenance window. we only have a quiet period sunday 0200-0500 our timezone. is that workable for an initial rehearsal?
06:55 Liz Chen: doable. we'll propose a rehearsal on 2027-03-25 02:30-03:30 local. that's the short maintenance window you mentioned.
07:20 Maya Ortiz: who owns rollback if the canary fails? do you automatically flip back to hosted? we need to know pre and post checks.
07:35 Ravi Kapoor: by default the policy is automated rollback to the prior capacity tier; we support manual abort as well. rollback steps: stop traffic to new pool, re-route, invalidate prefix cache if needed, and notify via webhook. we'll document exact steps in the runbook.
08:10 Liz Chen: for governance we recommend a go/no-go call with product, ops, and security on the morning after canary stress — should be less than 2 hours.
08:38 Tomás Rivera: any special network requirements for the private deployment? NAT gateway sizing? we saw egress spikes in previous runs.
08:53 Ravi Kapoor: sizing depends on token throughput — we'll model egress per token and share a spreadsheet. also recommend enabling batching at the API layer to reduce egress.
09:20 Maya Ortiz: pricing question — you mentioned cost per 1M tokens. can you break down committed vs burst pricing if we go dedicated?
09:37 Liz Chen: yes, i'll send a commit vs burst matrix. committed (reserved) capacity lowers per-token but you pay for idle. burst is pay-as-you-go but higher per token. we'll show sample numbers based on your 90th percentile usage.
10:05 Hannah Li: security: need to see SOC2 attestation and if you support customer-managed keys (CMKs).
10:18 Liz Chen: we do support CMKs via KMS/HSM, and SOC2 Type II is available, i'll attach the cert.
10:40 Maya Ortiz: ok timeline recap — you want to run the stress canary by 2027-03-21, rehearsal on 03-25, and final go decision on 03-28?
10:55 Ravi Kapoor: sounds right. can we make the internal go/no-go decision checklist explicit? i can draft it tonight and share.
11:12 Maya Ortiz: yes please. also include fallout actions for partial degradation — e.g., degrade to smaller model or increase quantization.
11:30 Tomás Rivera: curious on degradation strategy, do you have an automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant when latency spikes?
11:45 Ravi Kapoor: yes, smart routing can fall back to a compatible model variant in the same family. we toggle versions via policy and can set soft thresholds. there is some repro cost, we measure the quality delta.
12:10 Liz Chen: okay let's talk runbook structure. Ravi will own the runbook draft split by steps: pre-cutover checks, canary ramp plan, failure modes and rollback, post-cutover validation. We'll include playbooks for networking, and a checklist for security.
12:40 Ravi Kapoor: i'll include curl examples, trace IDs, sample alerts and Prometheus queries.
13:05 Hannah Li: on audit logs — do you redact identifiers before shipping? we can't send PHI in the payload.
13:22 Ravi Kapoor: we can mask payloads and only send metadata or hash of content. full payload retention is opt-in and can be disabled; we'll confirm default retention policy.
13:48 Maya Ortiz: okay one more — latency SLO: p95 target of 350ms — are we confident under 2x load?
14:05 Ravi Kapoor: with batching and the autoscale config we tested, p95 rose to 320ms under simulated 2x for 30 minutes. at 3x we saw p95 ~480ms and would recommend a different routing policy.
14:30 Tomás Rivera: can we schedule a joint load test with your infra and our SREs? we want to run k6 and Gatling scripts.
14:45 Liz Chen: yes, we'll pair. ryan from SRE on our side will join the run.
15:12 Maya Ortiz: question about A/B testing during canary — we want to split traffic for a subset of users to validate new prompt templates. can Redwood do header-based routing to route 10% of users?
15:28 Ravi Kapoor: header-based route is supported. we can do cookie or header id and route that bucket through the canary variant. results will be in the product dashboard.
15:52 Hannah Li: any compliance artifact for that routing? is it auditable?
16:05 Liz Chen: yes every routing decision is traced and we export traces and audit logs; we'll include the export path in the docs.
16:30 Maya Ortiz: ok back to the go/no-go timeline — we need a checklist, dashboards, security signoff, and rehearsal. if all green, we aim to go live 03-28. does that still feel realistic?
16:48 Ravi Kapoor: yes, given the tests complete. but if the 2x canary shows any SLO breach we'll extend the canary and escalate.
17:05 Tomás Rivera: what about cost controls during the canary to avoid bill shock?
17:18 Liz Chen: set a per-hour spend cap on the routing policy and alerts on burn-rate. we'll add that to the runbook — recommended caps included.
17:40 Maya Ortiz: okay i'm comfortable. final ask — please make the runbook consumable for our on-call engineers, not just managers.
17:55 Ravi Kapoor: will do, we'll include run commands and quick rollback commands.
18:10 Liz Chen: wrap-up: Ravi will push canary runbook draft by 03-20, liz will send pricing + security docs by 03-18, and customer to confirm go/no-go attendees by 03-19. next sync scheduled after the canary run (tentatively 2027-03-22). thanks all.
18:30 Maya Ortiz: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
18:35 (recording ends)
